The consensus was that Fed's Logan and Fed's Hammack would prefer a rate increase, but we also got Fed's Kashkari joining the dissenting camp.

The commerce department reported on Thursday that growth in US gross domestic product (GDP) – the nation’s output of goods and services – decelerated from 2.1% in the first three months of 2026 and came in below economists’ expectations.

The commerce department also said on Thursday that its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the measure of inflation favored by the Fed, rose 3.7% last month from June 2025, down from a 4.1% year-over-year increase in May.

The first GDP reading of this year captured the effects of just a month of war, but indicated that consumer spending was starting to slow as prices started to creep up.
